message.reasoning:
need to generate a JUnit 4 test file HttpConnectionTest.java that comprehensively tests all methods in HttpConnection. Since HttpConnection interacts with network, we need to mock HttpURLConnection to avoid real network. Use a custom URLStreamHandler that returns a mock HttpURLConnection. Also test static methods encodeUrl, encodeMimeName, request building, header handling, cookie handling, data handling, request body, postDataCharset, etc. Also test Response parsing maybe using a fake InputStream with simple HTML.

We can use Mockito to mock HttpURLConnection and related classes. However we also need to handle static methods like HttpConnection.Response.execute which uses URL.openConnection(). We'll create a URL with custom handler that returns our mock connection.

Test cases:

1. encodeUrl replaces spaces with %20. Provide a URL with space.

2. encodeMimeName replaces double quotes.

3. HttpConnection.connect(url).url(...).userAgent(...).header(...).cookie(...).data(...).requestBody(...).postDataCharset(...). Verify request fields.

4. Test Request methods: proxy, timeout, maxBodySize, followRedirects, ignoreHttpErrors, ignoreContentType, validateTLSCertificates, etc.

5. Test Base header methods: addHeader, header retrieval, case-insensitivity, removeHeader, hasHeader, hasHeaderWithValue.

6. Test cookie methods: set, get, hasCookie, removeCookie.

7. Test KeyVal creation and chaining.

8. Test Response parsing: simulate a response with content type text/html and body "<html><body>Hello</body></html>". Ensure parse returns Document with text.

We need to mock HttpURLConnection behavior: setRequestMethod, getResponseCode, getInputStream, getHeaderFieldKey/Value, getContentType, getURL, getHeaderFields etc. Simplify: we can subclass HttpURLConnection (abstract) and implement needed methods.

Create a class MockHttpURLConnection extends HttpURLConnection with fields for method, responseCode, headers map, inputStream, etc.

In test, create URL using new URL(null, "http://example.com/", new URLStreamHandler() { public URLConnection openConnection(URL u) { return mockConn; } });

Set up mockConn to return appropriate values.

Then call HttpConnection.connect(url).method(Method.GET).execute(); It will go through Response.execute, which uses our mock connection.

Test that Response statusCode etc. Also test that body() returns correct string.

Edge cases: test redirect handling: maybe simulate a redirect response with Location header and see that followRedirects works. Might be complex due to recursion; we can test that when followRedirects false, it does not follow.

Simplify: test response when ignoreHttpErrors false and status code 404 triggers HttpStatusException.

We can set response code 404 and no ignoreHttpErrors; expect exception.

Test ignoreHttpErrors true: should not throw.

Test unsupported content type: set content type "application/octet-stream", ignoreContentType false -> expect UnsupportedMimeTypeException.

Test with ignoreContentType true -> no exception.

Ok.

Implement tests using JUnit 4 annotations @Test, @Before.

We'll need to import Jsoup classes; assume they are on classpath.

We'll use org.jsoup.helper.HttpConnection, org.jsoup.Connection, org.jsoup.parser.Parser, org.jsoup.nodes.Document, org.jsoup.HttpStatusException, org.jsoup.UnsupportedMimeTypeException.

Write test class.

Make sure to include ###Test START## at top and ###Test END## at bottom.

Now produce answer.
